blocks.x: Dynamic Pricing & Revenue Intelligence: the composed architecture, the platforms underneath and the metric the program is judged on.
The problem this solution exists for
Pricing decisions inherit batch demand models and competitor snapshots; elasticity is estimated, markdown timing is instinctive, and revenue leaks are discovered in the margin bridge.
Our approach

Streaming demand sensing feeds elasticity models per SKU-location; price and markdown policies run through a decision hub with guardrails and challenger testing; every action carries measurement so the policy improves each cycle.
Components
Platform stack
The solution runs on Dataq Nexus and Dataq Forge: Enterprise decisions in milliseconds — with a full evidence trail for each decision. The governed data estate every AI program needs.
How it runs in an engagement

items: Baseline metrics for this problem locked with owners; current-state decision/data flow mapped in two weeks.
Gated pilot on bounded scope with the testable criterion agreed by finance before the first build sprint.
Staged rollout on the platform stack with SLOs, replay evidence and operator enablement.
Challenger models and policies quarterly; conformance monitoring; annual value audit against baseline.

items: Reference architecture adapted to your estate, with the integration contracts itemized.

blocks.x: Prerequisites and data readiness
Prerequisites are modest and named: governed access to the core data sources, a named executive sponsor and a control owner, and a sandbox where the proof can run on real records.
Proof

KYC refresh backlog cleared: 70% faster cycles with agentic file assembly

blocks.x: Industry fit

Deployed across Retail & Consumer Goods, Manufacturing & Industrial, Agriculture & Food Systems. Each industry play adjusts the regulatory frame, the integration surface and the KPI set — the pattern stays, the physics changes.
Outcomes we commit to
How a delivery runs

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
